BacksolveOptions.k#summary.en: Number of rows and columns of the triangular matrix to use (its top-left `k` x `k` block). Default: the number of columns of the matrix.

BacksolveOptions.transpose#summary.en: Solve `t(r) y = x` instead of `r y = x`. Default: `false`.

BacksolveOptions.upperTri#summary.en: Use the upper triangle of the matrix. Default: `true` for `backsolve`, `false` for `forwardsolve`. R's `upper.tri`.

Chol2InvOptions.size#summary.en: Number of rows and columns of `x` to use (its top-left `size` x `size` upper triangle). Default: the number of columns of `x`.

CholOptions.pivot#summary.en: Use diagonal pivoting (largest remaining diagonal first), which also works for positive semi-definite matrices. Default: `false`.

CholOptions.tol#summary.en: Stopping tolerance for the pivoted decomposition. A negative value means `n * eps * max(diag(x))`. Default: `-1`. Used only with `pivot: true`.

CholPivotResult.r#summary.en: The upper triangular factor `R`, such that `x[pivot, pivot] = t(R) R` for positive semi-definite `x`. Rows from `rank` on are 0.

CholPivotResult.rank#summary.en: The number of columns factored before the decomposition stopped (R's `attr(, "rank")`).

Determinant#summary.en: Result of {@link determinant}: the determinant equals `sign * modulus` (or `sign * exp(modulus)` when `logarithm` is `true`).

Determinant.logarithm#summary.en: Whether `modulus` is on the log scale.

Determinant.modulus#summary.en: The absolute value of the determinant, or its natural logarithm when `logarithm` is `true`. `-Infinity` (or 0) for an exactly singular matrix.

Determinant.sign#summary.en: The sign of the determinant (`1` or `-1`).

DiagOptions.ncol#summary.en: Number of columns of the matrix built from a vector or a number (R's `ncol`). Default: `nrow`.

DiagOptions.nrow#summary.en: Number of rows of the matrix built from a vector or a number (R's `nrow`). Default: the length of the vector.

EigenOptions.onlyValues#summary.en: Compute only the eigenvalues. Default: `false`. R's `only.values`.

EigenOptions.symmetric#summary.en:
Treat the matrix as symmetric (only its lower triangle is then used). Default: detected automatically,
like R's `isSymmetric()` (relative difference between the matrix and its transpose at most `100 * eps`).

EigenResult.values#summary.en:
The eigenvalues (their real parts if complex). Sorted in decreasing order for a symmetric matrix, and by
decreasing modulus otherwise (within a complex conjugate pair, the one with positive imaginary part comes first).

EigenResult.valuesIm#summary.en: The imaginary parts of the eigenvalues. Present only for a non-symmetric matrix with complex eigenvalues.

EigenResult.vectors#summary.en: The eigenvectors as columns (array of rows; real parts if complex), each of unit length. Omitted with `onlyValues: true`.

EigenResult.vectorsIm#summary.en: The imaginary parts of the eigenvectors. Present only when `valuesIm` is present (and vectors were computed).

ExpmOptions.method#summary.en:
`"Higham08.b"` (default): Higham's scaling and squaring with Padé approximants after balancing (LAPACK's
`dgebal`, permutation then scaling). `"Higham08"`: the same without balancing. `"Pade"` and `"Taylor"` (and
`"PadeO"`, `"TaylorO"`, which compute the same): scaling and squaring with a diagonal Padé approximant or a
Taylor polynomial of degree `order` (Shapira and Firth's code in the expm package).

ExpmOptions.order#summary.en:
Degree of the Padé approximant or the Taylor polynomial (a positive integer up to 2147483647, R's integer range,
and with order * (n^3 + 64) at most 2^31 for an n x n matrix, a bound on the time), used only by `"Pade"`,
`"Taylor"`, `"PadeO"` and `"TaylorO"`. Default: 8.

KappaOptions.exact#summary.en: Compute the condition number exactly instead of estimating it. Default: `false`.

KappaOptions.method#summary.en:
Estimation method when `exact` is `false`: `"qr"` applies LINPACK's `dtrco` estimate to the `R` factor of
the QR decomposition (of the transpose if `z` is wide); `"direct"` uses `1 / rcond(z)`. Default: `"qr"`.

KappaOptions.norm#summary.en:
The norm. Default: `"2"` when `exact` is `true`, otherwise `"1"`. With `exact: true`, `"2"` uses the singular
values and other norms use `norm(z) * norm(solve(z))`. With `exact: false`, as in R: the estimates through a
triangular factor (`method: "qr"`, or `"direct"` with `triangular: true`) use the infinity norm only for `"I"`
written exactly so and the 1-norm for any other norm (R warns for norms other than `"1"`, `"O"` and `"I"`, and
for `"2"`); `method: "direct"` without `triangular` accepts `"1"`, `"O"` and `"I"` in either case and throws for
any other.

KappaOptions.triangular#summary.en: Treat `z` as triangular and use only its triangle given by `uplo`. Default: `false`. Has an effect only with `method: "direct"` (as in R).

KappaOptions.uplo#summary.en: With `triangular: true`, use the upper (`"U"`) or lower (`"L"`) triangle. Default: `"U"`.

LuResult#summary.en: Result of {@link lu}: `x = P L U`.

LuResult.L#summary.en: Unit lower triangular (m x min(m, n)).

MatrixInput#summary.en:
A matrix given as an array of rows. Each row may be a plain array or a `Float64Array`;
all rows must have the same length. A matrix with zero rows is treated as 0 x 0.

MatrixOptions.byrow#summary.en: Fill by rows instead of by columns (R's default). Default `false`.

MatrixOptions.ncol#summary.en:
Number of columns (R's `ncol`). Default: the length of the data divided by `nrow` (rounded up), or 1 when `nrow`
is not given either.

MatrixOptions.nrow#summary.en:
Number of rows (R's `nrow`). Default: the length of the data divided by `ncol` (rounded up), or the length of
the data when `ncol` is not given either.

NormOptions.type#summary.en:
Which norm to compute (a single character, case-insensitive). Default: `"O"`.
- `"O"` or `"1"`: one norm, the maximum absolute column sum
- `"I"`: infinity norm, the maximum absolute row sum
- `"F"` or `"E"`: Frobenius norm
- `"M"`: the maximum absolute value of the elements
- `"2"`: spectral norm, the largest singular value

NormType#summary.en:
Matrix norm type for {@link norm}: `"O"`/`"1"` (one norm), `"I"` (infinity norm), `"F"`/`"E"` (Frobenius),
`"M"` (maximum modulus) or `"2"` (spectral norm). Case-insensitive, as in R.

Operand#summary.en: A vector (plain array) or a matrix (array of rows).

OuterFun#summary.en: The operation of {@link outer}: `"*"`, `"+"`, `"-"`, `"/"`, `"^"` or a function of two numbers.

PrcompOptions.center#summary.en: Centre the columns (default `true`), or subtract the given values.

PrcompOptions.rank#summary.en:
The number k of components to keep in `rotation` and `x` (R's `rank.`): `min(trunc(rank), nrow, ncol)`. It must
be finite with a positive integer part. Default: all `min(nrow, ncol)`. `sdev` always has all of them, as in R.

PrcompOptions.scale#summary.en: Scale the columns to unit variance (default `false`), or divide by the given values.

PrcompOptions.tol#summary.en:
Drop the components whose standard deviation is at most `tol` times that of the first: `rotation` and `x` keep
the components with `sdev > sdev[0] * tol` if they are fewer than k. Default: none are dropped.

PrcompResult.rotation#summary.en: Loadings: the eigenvectors as columns (variables x components kept).

PrcompResult.sdev#summary.en: Standard deviations of the principal components.

PrcompResult.x#summary.en: Scores: the data in the coordinates of the components (observations x components kept).

QR#summary.en:
A QR decomposition returned by {@link qr}, in R's compact form. Pass it to {@link qrQ}, {@link qrR},
{@link qrCoef} and the other `qr*` functions.

QR.qr#summary.en: Compact form: the upper triangle holds `R`; the part below the diagonal holds the Householder vectors that represent `Q`.

QR.qraux#summary.en:
Auxiliary information about `Q`: the leading elements of the Householder vectors for the LINPACK method (`ncol`
elements), `tau` for the LAPACK method (one per reflection, `min(nrow, ncol)` elements).

QR.rank#summary.en: The computed rank of the matrix. Always `min(nrow, ncol)` for `lapack: true`.

QR.useLapack#summary.en: Whether the decomposition was computed with `lapack: true` (R's `attr(, "useLAPACK")`).

QROptions.lapack#summary.en:
Use LAPACK-style full column pivoting (R's `LAPACK = TRUE`). The rank is then always `min(nrow, ncol)`
and is not detected. Default: `false` (R's LINPACK-style limited pivoting with `tol`).

QROptions.tol#summary.en:
Tolerance for detecting linear dependence: a column whose remaining norm falls below `tol` times its
original norm is moved to the right end and reduces the rank. Default: `1e-7`. Used only when `lapack` is `false`.

QRQOptions.complete#summary.en: Return the full `n` x `n` matrix `Q`. Default: `false`, which returns the first `min(n, p)` columns (`n` x `min(n, p)`).

QRQOptions.dvec#summary.en: Diagonal of a diagonal matrix that `Q` is multiplied by on the right. Its length must equal the number of returned columns. Default: all ones.

RcondOptions.norm#summary.en: The norm: `"O"` or `"1"` (one norm) or `"I"` (infinity norm). Default: `"O"`.

RcondOptions.triangular#summary.en: Treat `x` as triangular and use only its triangle given by `uplo`. Default: `false`.

RcondOptions.uplo#summary.en:
With `triangular: true`, use the upper (`"U"`) or lower (`"L"`) triangle; any other value is an error for a
square matrix (a non-square matrix uses R of its QR decomposition, as in R). Default: `"U"`.

SchurResult#summary.en: Result of {@link schur}: `x = Q T Q'`.

SchurResult.T#summary.en: The upper quasi-triangular factor (array of rows).

SchurResult.valuesIm#summary.en: Imaginary parts of the eigenvalues (0 for real ones; a complex pair has the positive one first).

SchurResult.valuesRe#summary.en: Real parts of the eigenvalues, in the order of T's diagonal blocks.

SolveOptions.tol#summary.en:
Tolerance for detecting singularity: throws if the estimated reciprocal condition number (one norm) is
smaller than this. A value of 0 or less disables the check. Default: `Number.EPSILON`.

SvdOptions.nu#summary.en: Number of left singular vectors to compute. Default: `min(nrow, ncol)`. A fraction is truncated toward zero, and values above the number of rows (`Infinity` included) are reduced to it. Negative values and `NaN` are errors.

SvdOptions.nv#summary.en: Number of right singular vectors to compute. Default: `min(nrow, ncol)`. A fraction is truncated toward zero, and values above the number of columns (`Infinity` included) are reduced to it. Negative values and `NaN` are errors.

SvdResult#summary.en: Result of {@link svd}: `x = u %*% diag(d) %*% t(v)`.

SvdResult.d#summary.en: The singular values, in decreasing order.

SvdResult.u#summary.en: The left singular vectors as columns (`nrow` x `nu`, array of rows). Omitted when `nu` is 0.

SvdResult.v#summary.en: The right singular vectors as columns (`ncol` x `nv`, array of rows). Omitted when `nv` is 0.

VectorOrMatrix#summary.en:
A vector or a matrix (array of rows). Used for arguments that accept either, such as the
right-hand side of `backsolve`; a vector is treated as a one-column matrix, as in R.

add#summary.en:
Element-wise sum with R's recycling (a shorter vector is recycled down the columns of a matrix). Equivalent to
R's `+`.

backsolve(0)#@returns.en: The solution `y`, a vector of length `k`.

backsolve(0)#summary.en:
Solves the triangular system `r y = x` with a vector right-hand side. Equivalent to R's `backsolve()`.

Only the top-left `k` x `k` triangle of `r` (upper by default) and the first `k` elements of `x` are used.
Throws if a diagonal element is exactly zero.

backsolve(1)#@param x.en: The right-hand side matrix (array of rows); only its first `k` rows are used.

backsolve(1)#@returns.en: The solution `y`, a matrix with `k` rows.

backsolve(1)#summary.en: Solves the triangular system `r y = x` with a matrix right-hand side.

backsolve(2)#@param x.en: The right-hand side, a vector or a matrix.

backsolve(2)#@returns.en: A vector if `x` is a vector, otherwise a matrix with `k` rows.

backsolve(2)#summary.en: Solves the triangular system `r y = x`.

cbind(0)#summary.en:
Combine vectors and matrices as columns. Equivalent to R's `cbind()`. Vectors are recycled to the number of rows.
Given data frames (objects of columns), puts their columns side by side, as R's `cbind()` of data frames: all must
have the same number of rows, and a column name may occur only once.

cbind(1)#summary.en:
Combine vectors and matrices as columns. Equivalent to R's `cbind()`. Vectors are recycled to the number of rows.
Given data frames (objects of columns), puts their columns side by side, as R's `cbind()` of data frames: all must
have the same number of rows, and a column name may occur only once.

chol(0)#@param x.en: A square symmetric positive definite matrix (array of rows).

chol(0)#@returns.en: The upper triangular factor `R` as an array of rows.

chol(0)#summary.en:
Cholesky decomposition. Equivalent to R's `chol()`.

Returns the upper triangular `R` with `x = t(R) R`. Only the upper triangle of `x` is used (symmetry is
not checked), and the lower triangle of the result is zero. Throws if `x` is not positive definite.

chol(1)#@param x.en: A square symmetric matrix (array of rows). Only the upper triangle is used.

chol(1)#@returns.en: The factor, the 0-based pivot and the rank. See {@link CholPivotResult}.

chol(1)#summary.en:
Pivoted Cholesky decomposition, as R's `chol(x, pivot = TRUE)`.

Does not throw for rank-deficient (positive semi-definite) matrices; check `rank` instead (R gives a
warning). As in R 4.6, the trailing submatrix of `r` from row and column `rank` on is 0, so that
`x[pivot, pivot] = t(R) R` holds for a positive semi-definite `x`.

chol(2)#@param x.en: A square symmetric matrix (array of rows).

chol(2)#@returns.en: The factor `R`, or a {@link CholPivotResult} when `pivot` is `true`.

chol(2)#summary.en: Cholesky decomposition, with or without pivoting.

chol2inv#@param x.en: The upper triangular Cholesky factor `R` (array of rows), e.g. from {@link chol}. A vector is treated as a one-column matrix.

chol2inv#@returns.en: The symmetric inverse matrix (`size` x `size`) as an array of rows.

chol2inv#summary.en:
Inverse of a matrix from its Cholesky factor: computes `(t(R) R)^-1`. Equivalent to R's `chol2inv()`.

Only the upper triangle of the top-left `size` x `size` block of `x` is used. Throws if a diagonal element is zero.

crossprod#@param x.en: A matrix (array of rows) or a vector.

crossprod#@param y.en: A matrix or a vector with the same number of rows as `x`. Defaults to `x`.

crossprod#@returns.en: The product as an array of rows (`ncol(x)` x `ncol(y)`).

crossprod#summary.en:
Matrix cross-product `t(x) %*% y`, or `t(x) %*% x` when `y` is omitted. Equivalent to R's `crossprod()`.

A vector argument is treated as a one-column matrix.

det#summary.en: Determinant of a square matrix. Equivalent to R's `det()`.

determinant#@param options.en: `logarithm`: return the natural logarithm of the modulus. Default: `true`.

determinant#@returns.en: The modulus and sign. See {@link Determinant}.

determinant#summary.en:
Determinant as modulus and sign. Equivalent to R's `determinant()`.

Computed from an LU decomposition; the log modulus is the sum of the logs of the absolute diagonal elements.

diag#summary.en:
Matrix diagonals, diagonal matrices and identity matrices. Equivalent to R's `diag()`. It has three meanings: the
diagonal of a matrix (as a vector); the diagonal matrix of a vector of length 2 or more (its values recycled along the diagonal of an `nrow` x `ncol` matrix when given); and for a single
number n, the n x n identity matrix (with `nrow`/`ncol`, a matrix with that number on the diagonal).

divide#summary.en:
Element-wise quotient with R's recycling (a shorter vector is recycled down the columns of a matrix). Equivalent to
R's `/`.

eigen#@returns.en: The eigenvalues and eigenvectors. See {@link EigenResult}.

eigen#summary.en:
Eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a square matrix. Equivalent to R's `eigen()`.

Symmetric matrices use tridiagonalization and the implicit QL method; other matrices use Hessenberg reduction
and the Francis double-shift QR method, after balancing the matrix as LAPACK's `dgebal` does. R uses LAPACK, so eigenvalues agree up to rounding, but
eigenvector signs may differ from R (both are correct); for repeated eigenvalues the basis may differ.
Complex eigenvalues and eigenvectors are returned as separate real and imaginary parts (`valuesIm`,
`vectorsIm`). Each complex eigenvector is scaled to unit length with its largest component real and positive.
Throws on `NaN` or infinite values.

expm#summary.en:
Matrix exponential. Equivalent to `expm::expm(x, method, order)` in R. The methods are `"Higham08.b"` (the
default), `"Higham08"`, `"Pade"`, `"Taylor"`, `"PadeO"` and `"TaylorO"`.

`"Higham08.b"` and `"Higham08"` use the scaling and squaring method with Padé approximants of degree 3, 5, 7, 9 or
13 (Higham 2005), with or without balancing first, and throw if a linear system of the method is computationally
singular. The other methods use scaling and squaring with a Taylor polynomial or a diagonal Padé approximant of
degree `order` (the Padé quotient by the conjugate gradient squared method, as expm does).

forwardsolve(0)#@returns.en: The solution `y`, a vector of length `k`.

forwardsolve(0)#summary.en:
Solves the triangular system `l y = x` with a vector right-hand side. Equivalent to R's `forwardsolve()`.

Only the top-left `k` x `k` triangle of `l` (lower by default) and the first `k` elements of `x` are used.
Throws if a diagonal element is exactly zero.

forwardsolve(1)#@param x.en: The right-hand side matrix (array of rows); only its first `k` rows are used.

forwardsolve(1)#@returns.en: The solution `y`, a matrix with `k` rows.

forwardsolve(1)#summary.en: Solves the triangular system `l y = x` with a matrix right-hand side.

forwardsolve(2)#@param x.en: The right-hand side, a vector or a matrix.

forwardsolve(2)#@returns.en: A vector if `x` is a vector, otherwise a matrix with `k` rows.

forwardsolve(2)#summary.en: Solves the triangular system `l y = x`.

ginv#@param options.en: `tol`: relative tolerance for treating singular values as zero. Default: `sqrt(Number.EPSILON)`.

ginv#@returns.en: The generalized inverse (`ncol` x `nrow`) as an array of rows.

ginv#summary.en:
Moore-Penrose generalized inverse. Equivalent to `MASS::ginv()` in R.

Computed from the singular value decomposition; singular values not greater than `tol` times the largest
singular value are treated as zero.

kappa#summary.en:
Condition number of a matrix, estimated or exact. Equivalent to R's `kappa()`.

By default (as in R) this is the LINPACK estimate of the one-norm condition number, computed on the
triangular factor `R` of the QR decomposition. With `exact: true` and the default `norm: "2"`, it is the ratio
of the largest to the smallest singular value (computed with {@link svd}); `Infinity` if the matrix is singular.

kronecker#summary.en: Kronecker product. Equivalent to R's `kronecker()`. Two vectors give a vector.

lu#summary.en:
LU decomposition with partial (row) pivoting, `x = P L U`. Equivalent to R's `Matrix::lu()`. The factors are those
of `Matrix::expand(Matrix::lu(x))` (LAPACK's dgetrf). Throws on `NaN` or infinite values (`Matrix::lu` returns factors
with NaN or infinite values).

matMul#summary.en:
Matrix product. Equivalent to R's `%*%`. A vector is taken as a row or a column so that the product is defined
(two vectors give their inner product as a 1 x 1 matrix).

matrix#summary.en: Build a matrix from data, recycled to fill it. Equivalent to R's `matrix()`. Filled by columns unless `byrow`.

multiply#summary.en:
Element-wise product with R's recycling (a shorter vector is recycled down the columns of a matrix). Equivalent to
R's `*`. The matrix product is {@link matMul}.

norm#summary.en:
Matrix norm. Equivalent to R's `norm()`.

Returns `NaN` if the matrix contains `NaN`. For `type: "2"`, an infinite element is an error.

outer(0)#summary.en:
Outer product of two vectors: the matrix of `fun(x[i], y[j])`. Equivalent to R's `outer()`. `fun` is `"*"`
(default), `"+"`, `"-"`, `"/"`, `"^"` or a function of two numbers, given as the third argument or as the option
`fun` (giving both is a RangeError).

outer(1)#summary.en: Outer product of two vectors, with the operation in the options: `outer(x, y, { fun: "+" })`.

prcomp#summary.en:
Principal components of the columns of `x` (observations as rows). Equivalent to R's `prcomp()`. The sign of each
component is arbitrary, as in R.

qr#@returns.en: The decomposition in compact form. See {@link QR}.

qr#summary.en:
QR decomposition. Equivalent to R's `qr()`.

By default this uses Householder transformations with R's LINPACK-style limited column pivoting: columns that
are (nearly) linearly dependent on earlier ones, as judged by `tol`, are moved to the right end and the rank is
reduced. With `lapack: true` it uses LAPACK-style column pivoting (R's `LAPACK = TRUE`).

The default method throws on `NaN` or infinite values. With `lapack: true`, such input does not throw and the
result may differ from R's (which is not meaningful either).

qrCoef(0)#@param y.en: The response vector, with as many elements as the decomposed matrix has rows.

qrCoef(0)#@returns.en: The coefficient vector (one element per column of the decomposed matrix).

qrCoef(0)#summary.en:
Least-squares coefficients for a vector response. Equivalent to R's `qr.coef()`.

Coefficients are returned in the original column order. Coefficients of columns that were not used
(those after position `rank` in `pivot`) are `NaN` (R's `NA`). For a decomposition computed with
`lapack: true`, the first `min(nrow, ncol)` pivoted columns are used.

qrCoef(1)#@param y.en: The response matrix (array of rows), with as many rows as the decomposed matrix.

qrCoef(1)#@returns.en: The coefficients as an array of rows (one row per column of the decomposed matrix, one column per column of `y`).

qrCoef(1)#summary.en: Least-squares coefficients for each column of a matrix response.

qrCoef(2)#@param y.en: The response, a vector or a matrix.

qrCoef(2)#@returns.en: A vector if `y` is a vector, otherwise an array of rows.

qrFitted(0)#@param options.en: `k`: the number of pivoted columns to project onto (an integer from 0 to `rank`). Default: `q.rank`.

qrFitted(0)#@param y.en: The response vector, with as many elements as the decomposed matrix has rows.

qrFitted(0)#@returns.en: The fitted values as a vector.

qrFitted(0)#summary.en:
Least-squares fitted values for a vector response: the projection of `y` onto the space spanned by the
first `k` pivoted columns. Equivalent to R's `qr.fitted()`.

Not supported for a decomposition computed with `lapack: true` (throws).

qrFitted(1)#@param options.en: `k`: the number of pivoted columns to project onto (an integer from 0 to `rank`). Default: `q.rank`.

qrFitted(1)#@param q.en: A QR decomposition from {@link qr} (not `lapack: true`).

qrFitted(1)#@param y.en: The response matrix (array of rows), with as many rows as the decomposed matrix.

qrFitted(1)#@returns.en: The fitted values as an array of rows.

qrFitted(1)#summary.en: Least-squares fitted values for each column of a matrix response.

qrFitted(2)#@param options.en: `k`: the number of pivoted columns to project onto (an integer from 0 to `rank`). Default: `q.rank`.

qrFitted(2)#@param q.en: A QR decomposition from {@link qr} (not `lapack: true`).

qrFitted(2)#@param y.en: The response, a vector or a matrix.

qrFitted(2)#@returns.en: A vector if `y` is a vector, otherwise an array of rows.

qrQ#summary.en: Recovers the orthogonal matrix `Q` from a QR decomposition. Equivalent to R's `qr.Q()`.

qrQty(0)#@param y.en: A vector with as many elements as the decomposed matrix has rows.

qrQty(0)#summary.en: Computes `t(Q) %*% y` for a vector `y`. Equivalent to R's `qr.qty()`.

qrQty(1)#@param y.en: A matrix (array of rows) with as many rows as the decomposed matrix.

qrQty(1)#@returns.en: `t(Q) %*% y` as an array of rows.

qrQty(2)#@param y.en: A vector or a matrix with as many rows as the decomposed matrix.

qrQty(2)#@returns.en: A vector if `y` is a vector, otherwise an array of rows.

qrQy(0)#@param y.en: A vector with as many elements as the decomposed matrix has rows.

qrQy(0)#summary.en: Computes `Q %*% y` for a vector `y`. Equivalent to R's `qr.qy()`.

qrQy(1)#@param y.en: A matrix (array of rows) with as many rows as the decomposed matrix.

qrQy(1)#@returns.en: `Q %*% y` as an array of rows.

qrQy(2)#@param y.en: A vector or a matrix with as many rows as the decomposed matrix.

qrQy(2)#@returns.en: A vector if `y` is a vector, otherwise an array of rows.

qrR#@param options.en: `complete`: return all `n` rows instead of the first `min(n, p)`. Default: `false`.

qrR#summary.en:
Recovers the upper triangular matrix `R` from a QR decomposition. Equivalent to R's `qr.R()`.

The columns stay in pivoted order (as in R); use `q.pivot` to map them back.

qrResid(0)#@param y.en: The response vector, with as many elements as the decomposed matrix has rows.

qrResid(0)#summary.en:
Least-squares residuals for a vector response: `y` minus its projection onto the space spanned by the
first `rank` pivoted columns. Equivalent to R's `qr.resid()`.

Not supported for a decomposition computed with `lapack: true` (throws).

qrResid(1)#@param q.en: A QR decomposition from {@link qr} (not `lapack: true`).

qrResid(1)#@param y.en: The response matrix (array of rows), with as many rows as the decomposed matrix.

qrResid(1)#@returns.en: The residuals as an array of rows.

qrResid(1)#summary.en: Least-squares residuals for each column of a matrix response.

qrResid(2)#@param q.en: A QR decomposition from {@link qr} (not `lapack: true`).

qrResid(2)#@param y.en: The response, a vector or a matrix.

qrResid(2)#@returns.en: A vector if `y` is a vector, otherwise an array of rows.

qrSolve#@param a.en: A matrix (array of rows) or a QR decomposition from {@link qr}.

qrSolve#@param b.en: The right-hand side, a vector or a matrix. Default: the identity matrix.

qrSolve#@param options.en: `tol`: the tolerance passed to {@link qr} when `a` is a matrix. Default: `1e-7`.

qrSolve#@returns.en: A vector if `b` is a vector, otherwise an array of rows.

qrSolve#summary.en:
Solves `a x = b` in the least-squares sense using a QR decomposition. Equivalent to R's `qr.solve()`.

Throws if the rank is less than `min(nrow, ncol)`. When `b` is omitted, returns the inverse of `a` (square
matrices only). For a wide matrix, coefficients of unused columns are set to 0 (as in R).

qrX#@param options.en:
`complete`: whether the default `ncol` is the number of rows (`true`) or `min(nrow, ncol)` (`false`, the default).
  `ncol`: the number of columns to return, from 0 to `max(nrow, ncol)`; columns beyond the original ones are taken
  from `Q` (as in R). A larger `ncol` is an error (R pads zero columns).

qrX#@returns.en: The reconstructed matrix as an array of rows.

qrX#summary.en:
Reconstructs the original matrix from a QR decomposition, with columns back in their original order.
Equivalent to R's `qr.X()`.

If the decomposition was pivoted, `ncol` smaller than the number of columns is an error (as in R).

rbind(0)#summary.en:
Combine vectors and matrices as rows. Equivalent to R's `rbind()`. Given data frames (objects of columns), stacks
their rows, as R's `rbind()` of data frames: all must have the same column names, matched by name (the result has
the first frame's column order).

rbind(1)#summary.en:
Combine vectors and matrices as rows. Equivalent to R's `rbind()`. Given data frames (objects of columns), stacks
their rows, as R's `rbind()` of data frames: all must have the same column names, matched by name (the result has
the first frame's column order).

rcond#@returns.en: The estimated reciprocal condition number, between 0 and 1.

rcond#summary.en:
Estimate of the reciprocal condition number of a matrix. Equivalent to R's `rcond()`.

Uses LAPACK's estimators (`dgecon` on the LU decomposition, or `dtrcon` for triangular matrices). For a
non-square matrix, the estimate is computed on the triangular factor `R` of its QR decomposition
(of the transpose if the matrix is wide). Returns 0 for an exactly singular matrix.

schur#@returns.en: `T`, `Q` and the eigenvalues read off `T`. See {@link SchurResult}.

schur#summary.en:
Real Schur decomposition of a square matrix. Equivalent to R's `Matrix::Schur(x)`.

Returns an orthogonal `Q` and an upper quasi-triangular `T` with `x = Q T Q'`. `T` has 1 x 1 diagonal blocks for
real eigenvalues and standardised 2 x 2 blocks `[[a, b], [c, a]]` (`b c < 0`) for complex conjugate pairs
`a ± sqrt(-b c) i`. The decomposition is not unique: the order of the diagonal blocks and the signs of `Q`'s
columns may differ from R's (both are correct). Throws on `NaN` or infinite values.

seq#summary.en:
Regular sequences. Equivalent to R's `seq()`. `seq(from, to)` steps by ±1; `by` steps by the increment, up to
`to`; `lengthOut` gives that many values, both ends exact. `from` or `to` may be omitted (`undefined`) when the
other two are given; `seq(n)` alone is `1, 2, ..., n`.

solve(0)#@param b.en: Omit (or pass `undefined`) to compute the inverse.

solve(0)#@returns.en: The inverse of `a` as an array of rows.

solve(0)#summary.en:
Inverse of a square matrix. Equivalent to R's `solve(a)`.

Uses an LU decomposition with partial pivoting. Throws if the matrix is exactly singular or if its estimated
reciprocal condition number is below `tol` (the check is skipped for matrices with `NaN` or infinite values).

solve(1)#@param b.en: The right-hand side vector, with as many elements as `a` has rows.

solve(1)#summary.en:
Solves the linear system `a x = b` for a vector `b`, as R's `solve(a, b)`.

Throws if `a` is exactly singular or its estimated reciprocal condition number is below `tol`.

solve(2)#@param b.en: The right-hand side matrix (array of rows), with as many rows as `a`.

solve(2)#@returns.en: The solution `x` as an array of rows.

solve(2)#summary.en: Solves the linear system `a x = b` for a matrix `b`.

solve(3)#@param b.en: The right-hand side, a vector or a matrix. Omit to compute the inverse.

solve(3)#@returns.en: A vector if `b` is a vector, otherwise an array of rows.

solve(3)#summary.en: Solves the linear system `a x = b`, or inverts `a` when `b` is omitted.

subtract#summary.en:
Element-wise difference with R's recycling (a shorter vector is recycled down the columns of a matrix). Equivalent to
R's `-`.

svd#@returns.en: The singular values and vectors. See {@link SvdResult}.

svd#summary.en:
Singular value decomposition. Equivalent to R's `svd()`.

Uses the Golub-Reinsch algorithm, while R uses LAPACK's `dgesdd`. Singular values agree with R up to
rounding, but the signs of singular vectors may differ from R (both are correct); for repeated singular
values the vectors may span the same subspace with a different basis. Singular vectors beyond
`min(nrow, ncol)` are a basis of the orthogonal complement and do not match R. Throws on `NaN` or infinite values.

t#summary.en: Transpose. Equivalent to R's `t()`. A vector becomes a 1-row matrix.

tcrossprod#@param x.en: A matrix (array of rows) or a vector.

tcrossprod#@param y.en: A matrix or a vector with the same number of columns as `x`. Defaults to `x`.

tcrossprod#@returns.en: The product as an array of rows (`nrow(x)` x `nrow(y)`).

tcrossprod#summary.en:
Matrix cross-product `x %*% t(y)`, or `x %*% t(x)` when `y` is omitted. Equivalent to R's `tcrossprod()`.

A vector argument is treated as a one-column matrix.
